assumptions: The reference is the FASTA or UCSC assembly named.
limits: No threshold and no verdict; gene models and dbSNP need the network.
bio.jane/contract.question: How well do the reads in this window agree with the reference beneath them?

description: Read an alignment window and say how well its reads agree with the reference underneath them, the way the pileup's own bar does: the compared and differing base counts, plus the RefSeq gene models and known dbSNP variants over the same window. The reference is a FASTA in this project or a public UCSC assembly, exactly as the panel offers it. There is no threshold and no verdict: a rate in the tens of percent almost always means the reads were aligned to a different assembly than the one asked for, and when the file declares its own reference length the answer says so as a fact rather than as a judgement.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alignment.description: which BAM or SAM in this project, by name. Unset, it is the project's only alignment — and it refuses rather than guessing when there is more than one.

gene_track.description: which NCBI RefSeq set the gene models come from. Only meaningful against a UCSC assembly. The default is one curated transcript per protein-coding gene, which carries no mitochondrial genes at all — RefSeq Curated does. Values: ncbiRefSeqSelect (RefSeq Select and MANE), ncbiRefSeqCurated (RefSeq Curated), ncbiRefSeq (RefSeq All), ncbiRefSeqPredicted (RefSeq Predicted).

locus.description: the window, as a locus string (`chrM:3,300-3,460`). Unset, it is the whole of the alignment's first reference — the window the panel opens on.

reference.description: what to compare against: a FASTA in this project by name, or a UCSC assembly id (`hg38`, `hg19`, `mm39` — the same list the panel's picker fetches). Unset is the panel's own default, No reference, and then only the window and its annotation are reported.

variants.description: also report the known dbSNP variants in the window. Off by default, as in the panel: it is a third layer over the reads and a dense window can hold thousands.

name: alignment_agreement

cautions.description: what this run earned: a reference whose length disagrees with the one the file declares, no-call bases counted as neither, and the window the numbers describe

compared.description: aligned bases that had a reference base to compare against — the denominator

conclusion.description: the reading in one sentence, generated from this run — the panel's own words

genes.description: the RefSeq models overlapping the window: symbol, accession, strand and bounds, as UCSC states them

noCall.description: aligned bases where one side is N — counted as neither, which is where this differs from an aligner's NM

pathogenic.description: how many of those ClinVar calls pathogenic

rate.description: differing aligned bases as a fraction of compared ones, 0 when nothing matched up

variants.description: the dbSNP records in the window when asked for: rsID, alleles, class, highest reported frequency and ClinVar significance

window.description: the window actually measured, as a locus string
